rules.statement: When a build or CI gate script gains a validation check, put the check in its own script or function that takes its inputs (such as the repository root or file list) as parameters, and add a test that runs every failure branch and a clean case against fixture files.
rules.why: If the repository's real inputs are all valid, nothing ever runs the failure branches. A mistake in the pattern or path could then leave a check that passes on anything, or one that blocks correct pull requests.
rules.check: Look for new failure branches in a build/gate script (duplicate detection, regex or prefix checks) that only run against the live repository, with no fixture-based test script that checks the exit code and output for each failing case.

rules.statement: Don't ask a GitHub Actions job that calls a reusable workflow to drop permissions such as `pages: write` or `id-token: write` when only a called job that is gated by `if:` uses them. First check the permissions the called workflow's jobs declare.
rules.why: The caller's grant is a ceiling, not a token: each called job only gets the permissions it declares. GitHub checks those against the ceiling when the run starts, before it evaluates `if:`, so narrowing the caller makes every run fail at start.
rules.check: Before reporting broad permissions on a `uses:` job, read the pinned called workflow. Confirm whether it sets `permissions: {}` at the top level and narrower permissions per job, and which job needs the elevated permission.

rules.statement: Don't report a non-constant-time comparison (such as `SequenceEqual`) of a secret or MAC in a documentation sample that deliberately shows the insecure usual code and has a comment saying it does so on purpose.
rules.why: Some guide samples exist to show the common, leaky pattern next to the safe one. Changing them would defeat the page's purpose.
rules.check: Before reporting, check whether the comparison sits inside a sample region for a page about how secrets leak or what not to do, and whether a nearby comment explains that the comparison is intentional.
